pr.title: Allow use of 'no_proxy' in the proxies argument
pr.description:
Add the ability to add 'no_proxy' and a value to the 'proxies' dictionary argument.

https://github.com/kennethreitz/requests/issues/2817

Closes gh-2817
pr.diff:

index 7983282a6d..51bad2caeb 100644
--- a/requests/sessions.py
+++ b/requests/sessions.py
@@ -231,13 +231,16 @@ def rebuild_proxies(self, prepared_request, proxies):
 
         :rtype: dict
         """
+        proxies = proxies if proxies is not None else {}
         headers = prepared_request.headers
         url = prepared_request.url
         scheme = urlparse(url).scheme
-        new_proxies = proxies.copy() if proxies is not None else {}
+        new_proxies = proxies.copy()
+        no_proxy = proxies.get('no_proxy')
 
-        if self.trust_env and not should_bypass_proxies(url):
-            environ_proxies = get_environ_proxies(url)
+        bypass_proxy = should_bypass_proxies(url, no_proxy=no_proxy)
+        if self.trust_env and not bypass_proxy:
+            environ_proxies = get_environ_proxies(url, no_proxy=no_proxy)
 
             proxy = environ_proxies.get(scheme, environ_proxies.get('all'))
 
@@ -651,7 +654,8 @@ def merge_environment_settings(self, url, proxies, stream, verify, cert):
         # Gather clues from the surrounding environment.
         if self.trust_env:
             # Set environment's proxies.
-            env_proxies = get_environ_proxies(url) or {}
+            no_proxy = proxies.get('no_proxy') if proxies is not None else None
+            env_proxies = get_environ_proxies(url, no_proxy=no_proxy)
             for (k, v) in env_proxies.items():
                 proxies.setdefault(k, v)

testCase.title: requests.utils.get_environ_proxies works when called with only a URL argument
testCase.preconditions: The requests library is installed and its internal utils module is imported directly, as some third-party integrations (e.g. request-building helper packages) do.
steps: Call get_environ_proxies('http://example.com') passing only the URL and no other argument
testCase.expectedResult: The call succeeds and returns a dictionary of proxy settings (an empty dictionary if no proxies apply), without raising any error.

provenance.note: PR #3865 merged 2017-02-10 changed requests/utils.py's get_environ_proxies(url) to get_environ_proxies(url, no_proxy) with no default value, requiring every caller to pass a second positional argument. This broke any code (including downstream packages) that called get_environ_proxies(url) with a single argument, raising a TypeError for a missing required positional argument. PR #4052 ('Fix regression in API caused by commit 85400d8d6751071ef78f042d1efa72bdcf76cc0e', i.e. PR #3865's merge commit) merged 2017-05-27 added a default value (no_proxy=None) to restore the original one-argument call signature.

pr.title: fix(parser): an edge case of parse_unit_value
pr.description:
Fixes the 1st issue of #17913

The other issue requires more changes. Maybe I don't know some background stories, but current `parse_unit_value` looks really weirdly complicated in my eyes. I may overhaul it in the future if I get more motivated.

Fixed a bug of duration/filesize parsing with numbers started by `.`, e.g. `.5sec`

testCase.title: A list literal containing a bare word that starts with a period parses as a string
testCase.preconditions: Nushell is installed and a REPL or script can be run.
testCase.expectedResult: The command returns the string '.foons' with no parser error.

provenance.note: PR #17923 merged 2026-03-29 changed parse_unit_value's entry condition in crates/nu-parser/src/parser.rs to accept any byte sequence starting with '.' as a potential duration/filesize literal, without requiring a following digit. This caused non-numeric dot-prefixed tokens such as '.foons' inside list literals to be misrouted into unit-value parsing and fail with a parser error. PR #18363, titled 'fix(parser): a regression of parse_unit_value where [.foons] not return early' and whose body states 'Fixes a regression introduced by #17923', merged 2026-06-08, tightened the condition to require bytes[1].is_ascii_digit() and added the regression test list_raw_string_unit_value_like asserting `[.foons] | get 0` returns '.foons'.

pr.title: Do not connect a sink for HEAD requests
pr.description: This PR was created in response to the test discussion in #2741: https://github.com/guzzle/guzzle/pull/2741#issuecomment-698808528

testCase.title: Sending a HEAD request with an Accept-Encoding header via the cURL handler completes successfully
testCase.preconditions: A Guzzle HTTP client is configured to use the default cURL handler.
steps: Create a Guzzle client with the header 'Accept-Encoding: gzip, deflate, br' set as a default header
Send a HEAD request to a reachable HTTP endpoint using that client
testCase.expectedResult: The request completes and returns a response object with a valid HTTP status code; no fatal error is raised.

provenance.note: PR #2778 merged 2020-09-29 changed CurlFactory::applyHandlerOptions() to skip setting $easy->sink entirely for HEAD requests when using the cURL handler. Issue #2799, titled 'Regression in #2778 - Call to a member function getSize() on null' (filed 2020-10-06), reports that a HEAD request with an Accept-Encoding header crashes with 'Call to a member function getSize() on null' at EasyHandle.php:84 because $easy->sink was left null; the reporter explicitly names #2778 as the cause and proposes reverting its commit 4552f37ba6027812d044aa4cdd8f8744b833bff4. PR #2804 ('Make sure the Request always has a body object'), merged 2020-10-09, states in its body 'It will revert changes in #2778 ... fix #2799', restoring an always-present sink/body object for HEAD requests.

pr.title: Format inserted/deleted maps in list assertions
pr.description: Solves #13624 When the elements are equal then we pass them as ast, when deleted or inserted we pass maps as %{a: 1, b: 2} and fall into inspect in safe_to_algebra. This pr changes maps to ast representation so it's formatted correctly in the function that handles maps.
pr.diff:
diff --git a/lib/ex_unit/lib/ex_unit/diff.ex b/lib/ex_unit/lib/ex_unit/diff.ex
index 05c2c7fda7e..f784d1a60b4 100644
--- a/lib/ex_unit/lib/ex_unit/diff.ex
+++ b/lib/ex_unit/lib/ex_unit/diff.ex
@@ -1142,9 +1142,22 @@ defmodule ExUnit.Diff do
   defp maybe_escape(other, %{context: :match}), do: other
   defp maybe_escape(other, _env), do: escape(other)
 
-  # We escape container types to make a distinction between AST
-  # and values that should be inspected. All other values have no
-  # special AST representation, so we can keep them as is.
+  # We escape container types to make a distinction between AST and values that
+  # should be inspected. Maps and structs without custom inspect implementation
+  # should not be inspected, convert it to ast.
+  # All other values have no special AST representation, so we can keep them as is.
+  defp escape(other) when is_map(other) do

testCase.title: ExUnit reports a clear match-failure diff for an assertion against a map containing an improper list
testCase.preconditions: An Elixir project using ExUnit for testing.
steps: Write a test containing the assertion: assert :foo = %{bar: [1 | 2]}
Run the test suite with mix test
testCase.expectedResult: The test fails with a standard 'match (=) failed' assertion error that shows the left value (:foo) and the right value (%{bar: [1 | 2]}); no additional crash occurs while formatting the failure.

provenance.note: PR #13954 merged 2024-11-17 changed ExUnit.Diff's escape/1 to convert map values via Map.to_list() and build_map_or_struct without escaping the resulting key/value pairs. Issue #14291 (filed 2025-02-20) reports a FunctionClauseError crash when formatting an assertion diff for a map containing an improper list; a reporter bisected the regression to commit a8c92060ea8fc9c0cfcec675d0752ffdd58699c9, which is PR #13954's merge commit. PR #14292 ('Fix regression when diffing nested improper lists'), merged 2025-02-21, adds '|> Enum.map(&escape_pair/1)' in lib/ex_unit/lib/ex_unit/diff.ex and adds a regression test asserting that `assert :foo = %{bar: [1 | 2]}` produces a proper match-failure diff instead of crashing.

pr.title: Format inserted/deleted maps in list assertions
pr.description: Solves #13624 When the elements are equal then we pass them as ast, when deleted or inserted we pass maps as %{a: 1, b: 2} and fall into inspect in safe_to_algebra. This pr changes maps to ast representation so it's formatted correctly in the function that handles maps.
